provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Young owner-run crews with striking floors; standard direction moves to a dark showroom combo because the floor finish is the product. No coating brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Cure times, one-day versus multi-day installs, UV yellowing, hot tyre pickup, chemical resistance, and why store-bought DIY kits peel
pageStructurePlus.why: Buyers arrive comparing coating types and have usually seen a failed DIY floor. Clear trade-offs justify the professional price.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Full-broadcast flake blends, solid colours, metallic epoxy, quartz, anti-slip texture options, and free sample chips by mail
pageStructurePlus.why: Colour is the fun decision and the one that stalls. A chart plus mailed chips moves the household to a yes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Diamond grinding versus acid etching, crack and spall repair, joint filling, moisture testing, and why prep decides whether a floor coating lasts
pageStructurePlus.why: Prep is the hidden difference between quotes. Showing the grinder and the repair work explains why the cheap bid fails.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Clearing the garage, grinding, repairs, base coat, flake broadcast, topcoat, when you can walk on it and when the car goes back in
pageStructurePlus.why: Owners need to know how long they lose the garage. A clear timeline removes the scheduling worry.

pageStructurePlus.section: Basements, patios, shops and commercial floors
pageStructurePlus.contains: Basement floor coatings, pool decks and patios, workshop and showroom floors, commercial kitchens and small warehouses
pageStructurePlus.why: The same crew can coat more than garages. A page per space captures the searches that aren't 'garage floor'.

designDirections.name: One-Day Floor
designDirections.bestFor: New coating crews selling one-day garage floors to homeowners who want a fast, clear quote
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo, used for the quote-first starter. Evergreen calms first-time buyers worried about peeling, and the page is a form and a call button.

designDirections.name: Showroom Garage
designDirections.bestFor: Coating crews with striking flake and metallic floors that sell on looks
designDirections.headlineSample: Garage floors that look like a showroom in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family combo on purpose: glossy flake and metallic floors read best on a dark ground, and basalt with a lime accent makes the finish the hero of the gallery.

designDirections.name: Collector's Garage
designDirections.bestFor: Premium crews coating collector garages, home gyms, metallic epoxy feature floors and showrooms
designDirections.headlineSample: Metallic and flake floors for {City}'s finest garages
designDirections.whyItFits: Noir and a Didone display feel like a car magazine spread, matching buyers who treat the garage as a showroom.

openers.line: Your listing shows glossy flake floors in the reviews but no website button. Someone planning a garage makeover wants colours and a quote, and there's nowhere to go.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: A floor coating page for that button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reels of fresh flake broadcasts are some of the best garage floor content in {City}. The only way to get a quote from them is a DM.
openers.hook: Find a flake broadcast or topcoat reel. Note how many comments ask for a price.
openers.linkLine: Those epoxy reels with a quote button underneath: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your coating site is a free one-pager with a builder banner. For a business that sells a showroom finish, the page undersells the floors.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a banner or broken form. Note which.
openers.linkLine: Same epoxy crew, a page that matches the floors: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your floor gallery loads slowly and crops the flake close-ups on my phone. The close-up is what sells a garage floor coating.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your epoxy gallery, sharp on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Getting a price from you means a DM and a wait. A form asking garage size and coating type gives a range and books the measure in one go.
openers.hook: Check profile and any site for prices or a form. If none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A garage floor quote by size and coating: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've coated garages in a lot of different flake blends, and people can't find them again once they scroll. A colour chart from your own floors would end the 'what was that grey one' messages.
openers.hook: Count the distinct flake colours in their grid. Mention two if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your flake blends as a colour chart: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention replacing peeling store-bought kits with a floor that's held up. That's the fear every buyer has, and the proof stays on Google.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one line about DIY failure or durability. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Those epoxy reviews where buyers decide: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring is when people empty their garages and decide the stained concrete has to go. The coating crews they find that month fill their summer.
openers.hook: Use in late winter and early spring. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: Ready for spring garage floor season: {demo-link}

openers.line: In cold months, people assume floor coatings can't be done. If you do polyaspartic in winter, a page saying so books jobs your competitors turn away.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted winter installs. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A winter garage floor coating page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring for the coating crew. Good grinder operators check how established an epoxy company looks before they sign on.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: An epoxy floor company page with careers: {demo-link}

openers.line: You coat garages across {City} and further out, but no page tells someone in {Neighborhood} you'll come. 'Garage floor coating' plus the town is the search.
openers.hook: Find towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the furthest.
openers.linkLine: A garage floor page for every town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: You've posted a basement and a workshop as well as garages. People searching for basement floor coatings never see those, because there's no page for them.
openers.hook: Only if they've posted non-garage floors. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A floor coating page for basements, patios and shops: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you stand behind your floors with a written warranty against peeling, it belongs on a page. That one line beats every DIY kit at the hardware store.
openers.hook: Only if they mention a warranty in posts or reviews. Never quote terms you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Your garage floor warranty, stated plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: Once one garage on a street gets a flake floor, the neighbours want theirs. Even those referrals search the epoxy company before calling.
openers.hook: Look for reviews like 'saw my neighbour's garage'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a neighbour's garage floor referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a beautiful floor, even flake coverage and a clean edge at the door. It should be the first thing a visitor sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest floor and name it: flake blend, space, and the town if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That garage floor, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a great looking floor, even flake and a clean edge.

I searched for garage floor coatings in {City} and found {Business Name} on social, but no site with a colour chart or a way to get a quote by garage size. I built a sample floor coating site to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case it got buried. Here's the sample floor coating site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has an epoxy versus polyaspartic page, a flake colour chart with sample chips, a prep page that explains grinding, and a quote form by garage size. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hey, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for floor coating companies in {City}. I messaged you a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries. Short version: I built a sample garage floor site for {Business Name} with a flake colour chart, a coating comparison and a quote by garage size, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range} depending on the colour chart and how many spaces you cover, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a coating crew your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, less than one two-car garage."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes one evening this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before spring garage clean-out season."

objections.objection: Instagram brings me plenty of work.
objections.handler: "It clearly does. Every person who sees a reel still has to DM you for a price. The site quotes them and shows the colour chart while you're grinding."

objections.objection: I'm on a franchise lead program already.
objections.handler: "Those leads are shared or capped. Your own site sends floor buyers straight to you, and the leads are yours."

objections.objection: People just compare me to the DIY kits on price.
objections.handler: "That's exactly why the prep and comparison pages matter. Once they see the grinder and the failed kits, your price makes sense."
"That's when to build it. It's ready for spring, and the winter polyaspartic page can bring jobs now."
"Good, use him. Happy to hand over the colour chart layout. If it stalls before spring, my offer stands."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, for the colour chart, comparison, prep page and quote form. Less than one garage floor."

bullets: Peg the build to one two-car garage floor, not an hourly rate.
The flake colour chart is the centrepiece; price it by the number of blends shown, not by page.
Quote forms that ask garage size, coating type and concrete condition are their own line.
Only add basement, patio or commercial pages for crews who already do that work.
Sample-chip mailing is cheap to add and closes jobs; include it when they keep chips on hand.
These are young crews watching cash; offer a smaller first build and add pages as the season pays.
